blocks.text: An eighteenth-century scholar said, "Water, which is essential for life, cost nothing. On the other hand, diamonds, which are essential for nothing, cost a lot." Unfortunately, the world has changed considerably since that remark was made. What was true over two hundred years ago is certainly no longer the case. What is still true, however, is a writer's comment, "When the well's dry, we know the worth of it." That is, we ignore it when we have it - unless we have too much of it, of course. Once there is a threat to its supply, however, water can quickly become the only thing that matter. We know only too well that, without it, there can be no life.
